newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power futures rebound amid Palo Verde news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power futures rebound amid Palo Verde news.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rebounded Wednesday from yesterday's losses amid news that a unit at the Palo Verde nuclear power plant was set to scale back output this weekend before its autumn refueling outage.

The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear power complex in Arizona will begin Sunday to slowly ramp down to between 60 and 80 percent power by September 6, when it scheduled to shut for refueling, the operator Arizona Public Service Co said.

In the aftermath of the market's focus on the outages at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) in southern California in recent days, brokers and traders said news of the coastdown program at Palo Verde 2 during late trading renewed concerns over reduced power supply in Southwest.
"It just made the market skittish," a West Coast electricity broker said.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 90 cents at $34.70 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high at $35.10.
September PV finished up 37 cents at $27.73. Deferred PV contracts ended down 15 to up 30 cents cents.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up 55 cents at $21.01 a MWh, nine cents below today's session high.
September COB finished up 48 cents at $21.50. Other active COB months ended down 15 to up 26 cents.

Some players attributed the factor behind today's rise to shortcovering ahead of August's expiration Monday, adding the return of the two SONGS units were more than adequate to make up for any reduced output at Palo Verde 2.
The 1,070 MW SONGS unit 2 at the in southern California reached 100 percent power midday Wednesday, while the neighboring 1,080 MW unit 3 was holding at 80 percent for post-refueling testing.
SONGS unit 3 was scheduled to resume full production before the end of the week.
Firm, peak power prices for Thursday at PV fell $1.50 to $27.50-28.50 a MWh, while those at COB were steady at $17.00-18.00.
Brokers and traders said market fundamentals in the West remained bearish in the short term due to rising spot supply and weak spot physical prices.
Technically, August PV will likely try to fill the chart gap at $35.10-35.25, while August COB would remain within its downside channel, market sources said.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were forcast at near to just above normal through the end of the week, moderating to near to just below normal into the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures were forecast at near or just above normal into the weekend.
